title: Baker and Mullin Rewrite TEG History at Boavista
title_candidates: Baker and Mullin Rewrite TEG History
Two Records Fall in a Single Morning
theme: Round 1 at Boavista delivers two once-in-a-competition rounds — Jon Baker's Trophy-best -9 and David Mullin's course-record 88 — while Henry Meller's 17th-hole disaster anchors the Wooden Spoon race before it has properly begun.
opening_hook: Boavista had already hosted three TEGs' worth of golf before Tuesday, but nothing in that history suggested Jon Baker was about to shoot the best round the competition has recorded — nor that David Mullin, in the same four-ball, would beat the course record while doing it.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker's net -9 stands as the best round recorded in TEG history to date
round_story.why_it_matters: Jon Baker's net -9 is, at the moment it was carded, the best round recorded anywhere in TEG's three-tournament history — a mark against which every future round will now be judged, and also comfortably the best of his own career.
round_story.shape: Baker opens steadily before a mid-round surge through the turn at the 7th to 9th, then goes through the 13th and 14th without dropping a gross shot; by the 18th his card reads -9, the best net round anyone has shot in TEG history and the best of his own career by some distance.
headline_candidates: Baker Sets a New Trophy Standard
round_story.standfirst: No one at Boavista's clubhouse had seen a net score like it, and the record books hadn't either.

race_story.subject: David Mullin's course-record round grabs the Green Jacket lead as Henry Meller sinks to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race
race_story.why_it_matters: With no prior rounds to react to, Round 1 sets the terms for all three competitions: Jon Baker's Trophy lead is already commanding, but the Green Jacket and Wooden Spoon tables both find new occupants in David Mullin and Henry Meller respectively.
race_story.shape: David Mullin's round builds quietly under the radar of Baker's fireworks, until his 88 gross is confirmed as a new Boavista course record and the best Gross round in TEG history — enough to put him two clear at the top of the Jacket table. At the other end, Henry Meller's outward frustrations curdle into a 12 at the 17th, the day's single worst hole, dropping him to the bottom of the Spoon table three shots adrift.
headline_candidates: A New Course Mark, A New Leader
Mullin Writes His Name Into Boavista
race_story.standfirst: Two competitions changed hands within a single round, and a third was already beyond saving for Henry Meller.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams's personal-best net round is undone by a catastrophic finish
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Buried in Gregg Williams's card is a personal-best net round — his lowest score yet in four TEGs — which makes the calamity that closes it all the harder to explain, and leaves him with the worst Gross return of the day.
discovered_storylines.shape: Williams's card is on course for his best net round in four TEGs until a quadruple bogey at the short 6th opens the door; three double- and triple-bogeyed holes from the 8th follow, before a finishing run from the 15th — triple, triple, triple, quadruple — turns a respectable book into the day's worst Gross score.
headline_candidates: Williams's Personal Best, Ruined by the Finish
discovered_storylines.standfirst: The card that started as his best round in four years ended as barely believable.

race_state_note: This is Round 1 of TEG 3, so every standing above reflects a single day's play rather than sustained form; the 8-shot Trophy gap and 2-shot Jacket gap could both move sharply on Wednesday.
